g1.label: 1. Renewable target by 2030
g1.why: The text says Scotland aims to generate 50% of total energy consumption from renewables by 2030.

g2.label: 2. Offshore wind target for 2040
g2.why: The text gives Scotland's offshore wind target for 2040 as 40 gigawatts.

g3.correct: it has long coastlines, exposed hillsides and strong winds
accept: it has long coastlines, exposed hillsides and strong winds
g3.label: 3. Why is Scotland suitable for wind energy?
g3.why: The text explains Scotland's long coastlines, exposed hillsides and strong winds make it suitable for wind energy.

g4.correct: they were destroyed by deforestation and farming
accept: they were destroyed by deforestation and farming
g4.label: 4. What happened to the Caledonian pine forests?
g4.why: The text says the ancient pine forests were destroyed by deforestation and farming.

g5.label: 5. Size of the Affric Highlands project
g5.why: The text gives the Affric Highlands rewilding project's size as 200,000 hectares.

g6.label: 6. What happens when peatlands are drained?
g6.why: The text says drained peatlands release greenhouse gases.

g7.correct: they absorb roughly twice as much per hectare
accept: they absorb roughly twice as much per hectare
g7.label: 7. Peatlands vs tropical rainforests
g7.why: The text says healthy peatlands absorb roughly twice as much carbon per hectare as rainforests.

g8.correct: they believe it threatens their livelihoods
accept: they believe it threatens their livelihoods
g8.label: 8. Why do some farmers oppose rewilding?
g8.why: The text says some farmers oppose rewilding because they believe it threatens their livelihoods.

g1.label: 1. If Scotland ___ its target (Type I)
g1.why: Type I conditionals use the present simple after ‘if’, with ‘will’ in the result clause.

g2.label: 2. The Highlands ___ in woodland today
g2.why: A past condition (‘had not been cut down’) with a present result (‘today’) is a mixed conditional using ‘would still be’.

g3.label: 3. If peatlands are restored, they ___ carbon (Type I)
g3.why: Type I conditionals use the present simple after ‘if’, with ‘will’ in the result clause.

g4.label: 4. ...if the government ___ more (Type II)
g4.why: Type II conditionals use the past simple after ‘if’, matching the result ‘would benefit’.

g5.label: 5. If farmers ___ earlier (Type III)
g5.why: Type III conditionals use the past perfect after ‘if’, paired with ‘would not have’.

g6.label: 6. If wind power continues to grow, Scotland ___ (Type I)
g6.why: Type I conditionals use the present simple after ‘if’, with ‘will’ in the result clause.

g7.label: 7. If there ___ no opposition (Type II)
g7.why: Type II conditionals with ‘be’ traditionally use ‘were’ for all subjects, matching ‘could expand’.

g8.label: 8. It ___ over 17 GW today
g8.why: A past condition (‘had not invested… twenty years ago’) with a present result (‘today’) is a mixed conditional using ‘would not have’.

g1.label: 1. Wind and solar are ___ energy
g1.why: ‘Renewable’ energy sources are naturally replenished and never run out.

g2.label: 2. Restoring ecosystems by reintroducing species
g2.why: ‘Rewilding’ is the process of restoring natural ecosystems and reintroducing native species.

g3.label: 3. Peatlands have been ___
g3.why: The text says centuries of drainage and farming have degraded Scotland's peatlands.

g4.label: 4. Villages have suffered from ___
g4.why: The text says Highland villages have suffered from depopulation as young people move to cities.

g5.label: 5. Variety of species in an area
g5.why: ‘Biodiversity’ is the variety of plant and animal species living in an area.

g6.label: 6. A forest provides an important ___
g6.why: A ‘habitat’ is the natural environment where animals like red squirrels live.

g7.label: 7. Burning fossil fuels produces ___
g7.why: Burning fossil fuels produces greenhouse gas emissions.

g8.label: 8. A ___ approach meets today's needs
g8.why: A ‘sustainable’ approach meets today's needs without compromising the future.
